components.cost_effect: One gradient query per update; O(np) table and O(p) running-sum storage; O(p) dense arithmetic per update.
components.goal: Reuse the latest available gradient from each fixed component without recomputing all n gradients.
components.key_estimate: Invariant s=sum_i y_i is maintained by replacement; performance is supplied by the linked Theorem, not by an unbiased-SGD assumption.
components.name: Gradient table and running sum
components.operation: Refresh one entry and replace its contribution in s before updating x.
components.requires: Stable component identities, repeatable exact gradient queries and stored entries.
transfer_checks: Re-establish the analysis for nonuniform sampling, noisy gradients, changing data, cyclic indices or altered initialization.
Structured-gradient storage reductions from Section 4.1 are outside this dense variant.

limitations.statement: Requires storage and indexed reuse of component gradients; the stored average is generally a biased gradient estimator.
This record does not transfer the guarantee to practical sampling, step-size or storage variants, and makes no unrestricted Oracle Complexity claim.

performance_links.scope_note: Only the zero-table branch under the full conditions in thm.P019.sag_rate.

variants.cost: K component-gradient calls and K uniform index draws. With the running sum, each dense update uses O(p) vector arithmetic in addition to the gradient computation; table storage is O(np), with O(p) extra running-sum/iterate/average storage. Dense zero initialization costs O(np) writes. Average accumulation costs O(p) per update. No function-value calls are needed by the fixed-budget implementation. Gradient evaluation cost itself is separately charged, not assumed O(1).
variants.implementation_details_ref: Eq.(5)–(6), p.3; Algorithm 1 and Section 4.1, p.10; Appendix B.1, p.35
variants.name: Zero-table SAG
variants.output: For the general convex guarantee return bar x^K=(1/K)sum_{t=0}^{K-1}x^t, accumulated before each update. For the strongly convex guarantee return x^K. Both are unconstrained points in R^p.
public_inputs: n and p; exact indexed component-gradient access; initial point x^0 in R^p; L>0 upper-bounding every component gradient Lipschitz constant; integer update budget K>=1
variants.query_and_update: For t=1,...,K: independently sample i_t uniformly from {1,...,n}; query v=grad f_{i_t}(x^(t-1)) once; set s <- s-y_{i_t}+v, y_{i_t} <- v, leaving other entries unchanged; set x^t=x^(t-1)-(alpha/n)s. Cache v so Algorithm 1's repeated gradient expression is evaluated once. This is Appendix B.1's indexing of Eq.(5)–(6).
variants.requirements: For the linked performance result: fixed differentiable convex f_i:R^p->R with globally L-Lipschitz gradients, g=(1/n)sum_i f_i attaining a minimum. Exact component gradients at chosen indices; independent uniform sampling with replacement. Strong convexity of g is required only for the linear-rate branch.
variants.state_and_initialization: Set x=x^0, y_i=0 in R^p for all i, and running sum s=0. No initial component-gradient evaluations. Allocate and initialize the table; keep a separate accumulator if returning the average.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Use constant alpha=1/(16L) for the linked Theorem. Stop after prescribed K updates. The rule needs neither mu nor sigma^2 nor x*. No certified online gap stopping rule is asserted.

use_restrictions: Dense basic Algorithm only; resource accounting is direct accounting of the stated implementation, not a new convergence claim.
Performance depends on the linked source-based Theorem; no independent Reviewer acceptance or publication claimed.
